Hey [~accountid:60913fd533a9410071c516c5] so let’s start with the rides.csv report

So the column *Price with VAT* totals to 6,349,300ngn & the column *Total cost of ride* totals to 6,347,000ngn. The difference is 2300ngn which is due to refunded orders processed on the same month (i.e. April). Here’s the order ids:

1114933932 - refund = 600ngn
1114593817 - refund = 1200ngn
1118694657 - refund = 500ngn

Total = 600 + 1200 + 500 = 2300ngn

Now the *Statement* shows 6,344,600ngn (and 4900 in refunds). You now might wonder why the refunds on the invoice is 4900 but above we say the refunds contribute only 2300 - well this is because one refund was processed in April (whereas the order took place in March hence it doesn’t surface on rides.csv report). This is the order for 2400ngn: 

[https://nigeria-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1105276945/1222758247|https://nigeria-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1105276945/1222758247]

So putting all of this together:

Price with VAT (6 349 300) - refunds processed this month (2300) = 6 347 000 (total cost of ride for the April report) - refund for older ride processed in April (2400) = 6 344 600 (equals to the invoice)

We already have a ticket open to fix those blanks in the report to actually say ‘this was refunded’ & hopefully this will help clear the confusion

Added four more cases of a similar crash when outgoing call is finished before the SinchClient initialisation has been finished. These three cases are a little bit different because during starting the client Sinch requested to renew the registration token and this is what made the start client window wider

{noformat}https://console.firebase.google.com/u/0/project/taxify-client/crashlytics/app/android:ee.mtakso.client/issues/305cb6df0864dc495b82102acd7f160f?time=last-seven-days&types=crash&versions=CA.39.0%20(1950);CA.38.0%20(1940);CA.38.0%20(1925);CA.38.1%20(1941);CA.37.2%20(1930);CA.37.2%20(1917)&sessionEventKey=6270290C000D00015A6631A3BA26549B_1671660622522188766
https://console.firebase.google.com/u/0/project/taxify-client/crashlytics/app/android:ee.mtakso.client/issues/87769818af96310c8b2c723af7db0ac2?time=last-seven-days&types=crash&versions=CA.39.0%20(1950);CA.38.0%20(1940);CA.38.0%20(1925);CA.38.1%20(1941);CA.37.2%20(1930);CA.37.2%20(1917)&sessionEventKey=6270192C036D000161424769DA7B7CA3_1671644686263208598
https://console.firebase.google.com/u/0/project/taxify-client/crashlytics/app/android:ee.mtakso.client/issues/c692c0873c54ee30f167efdba8c7c4dd?time=last-seven-days&types=crash&versions=CA.39.0%20(1950);CA.38.0%20(1940);CA.38.0%20(1925);CA.38.1%20(1941);CA.37.2%20(1930);CA.37.2%20(1917)&sessionEventKey=6272253902A600015B9FE155D9424C35_1672220668662436399{noformat}

So the scenario here is the following:

* Start outgoing call
* Start initialising {{SinchClient}}
* Sinch requests to renew credentials
* New credentials are obtained form the backend
* Provide new credentials to Sinch
* Sinch finishes registration and proceed to initialisation of the {{SinchClient}}
* User finishes the outgoing call
* {{SicnCallRepository}} proceed with starting the outgoing call and starts the foreground service
* Internal state doesn’t match because the call has been finished, so the {{IllegalVoipRepoStateException}} is thrown.
* Service never shows the notification because the internal call state is {{Idle}} and the system timeout exception makes the app to crash.

The following case doesn’t include refreshing credentials flow, but identical to the cases reported before for {{CA.35.0}} (i.e the outgoing call has been finished before the client is initialised. 2 seconds passed between user started the call and hung it up)

Campaigns team have the logic that rides flagged as fraudulent shouldn’t be taken into account for paying campaigns to drivers. From the Fraud perspective, the rides do look fake and were likely emulated by the driver with the sole purpose of reaching the campaign requirements. Did you check them? Having said that, the decision to pay or not the driver isn’t really a decision to be made by the Fraud team. If it was up to us, our advice would be to not compensate the driver. Driver campaigns are incentives we create to reward our good drivers. If they do fake rides to reach the campaign goals, doesn’t make sense for us to reward them. But again, it’s not our call to be made. More of a local team decision I would say.

{quote} The driver also wants to know if there’s anything in our Ts & Cs which prevents him from doing trips for the same rider in order to achieve a bonus?{quote}

About this, it’s a question to be made for the Legal team and not to Fraud. But pretty sure Legal will say that our campaigns can be flexible, where we can decide what to reward and what are the requirements we’ll ask for. It’s not a driver’s right, it’s an incentive. And if they have bad faith, doesn't make sense to reward.

Is it possible to add an additional clause that we have the right to terminate the contract when the employee will not receive the working permit? And possible to add" In case of early termination of the work permit by the relevant state authorities, the employment agreement would be considered as terminated on the same date" to cover any other situation._

# Before signing the contract on paper when they arrive in Baku, is it possible to sign the contracts digitally over Hellosign to start the relocation process? As per the laws e-signature, only e-signature approved by the certified centers in Azerbaijan are acceptable. Hellosign or Docusign is not advised to be applied in the case of employment documentation. Until that, whatever is signed may be considered as not enforceable. The practice is to get scanned copies first and then exchange hard-copies of the same scanned copies.

Where the foreign employee has local residence card, it is necessary to refer to ti as well. Common practice is that while obtaining work permit, residence permit is also obtained before signing the employment agreement. And therefore, all the details of these documents are specified in the employment agreement.
# Is it possible to prepare a legally binding document that indicates that we as a Company are ready to enter the employment agreement in case they receive the Work Permit as a guarantee and after getting permit we will sign the employment contract? The Company shall not sign any employment agreement with foreign employees without obtaining a work permit. Moreover, we suggest foreign employees not to attend office and not to be present at the workplace until obtaining the work permit. 

Please note that this ticket does not cover any issues that aren’t part of the employment contract, such as the relocation process and relocation agreement.

*Update*: 

Deduplicating documents and keeping names consistent is not straightforward.

Right now the file name is the concatenation of: \[_external id_]_\[_document type name_]_\[_document id_] 

For example: {{1507976_ng_vehicle_inspection_report_car_26989148.pdf}}_,_ corresponds to car id {{1507976}}, document type {{ng_vehicle_inspection_report_car}}, document {{26989148}}

When copying a document to a different type, the name would no longer be accurate. For example, when copying a document from _car application_ to _car,_ car filenames will be still referring to the _car application_ id. A similar problem would occur from driver registration → driver.

One possible solution would be setting the {{Content-Disposition}} header on the S3 file to set the downloading filename. See [here|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2611432/amazon-s3-change-file-download-name]

The important thing from the context perspective for you is that ever since we have been doing this branding bonus, without any agreement with fleet owners - so how it works right now. We have fleet owners, that have cars with our BOLT stickers, and every month we pay to them bonuses, if those cars complete a certain amount of rides. And such initiative is I think very popular across different countries and regions in which we operate. 

The thing is that we want to expand this branding bonus program in Poland and we want to have more cars with our stickers on. However, some fleet owners (not all of them) don’t want to participate in this bonus scheme without an agreement - Why? Because they are afraid that, for example, after a month we will decide to cut off this program and they will be left with our stickers without any award. On the other hand, from our perspective, it will be also beneficial for us to have such an agreement, because we will have some sort of exclusivity on cars with stickers (so similar case to car co-financing - co-financed cars have to deliver a certain level of rides monthly).

To conclude, it would be great to have a simple agreement, that we can use in situations when fleet owners are not convinced about our credibility when it comes to payouts for branding bonuses. And I don’t think that update of T&C will be helpful for us in this case.

Do I understand correctly that you would like us to add an issue type called “Active order issue”? If so, I am not entirely sure what the purpose of that would be. 

Can you please clarify the last paragraph also to me? I get a feeling I am misunderstanding the problem statement here a bit. 

_____

Overall every single contact we get from Eaters can be classified into 4 categories from an order lifecycle perspective: 

# Issue happens during an active order
# Issue happens before an order
# Issue happens after an order
# Issue is not related to an order

My guess here is that majority of our contact volumes actually come in during the active order, which would mean that we categorise majority of our CCPO into one issue type that is too general, because there are a million moving pieces during each active order which can all fail. So if we add this one issue type to cover everything, we end up with close to no insight whatsoever about what’s actually behind it. 

Our focus is to have the issue types “scenario-based” that are distinguishable yet general enough to cover different, but similar scenarios. Previously issue types were more detailed, but it came at the cost of accuracy. The current system is designed to regain that accuracy for mainly Supportability, but also to make sense for the customers.

Sharing my views on how its done with fleets in other regions:

* in markets where we do have dedicated fleet agreements (e.g. ES) we added branding bonus agreement to the special T&Cs we sign with bigger fleets. It sets amount of bonus and KPIs, commitment term, min-qualifying standards. But this makes sense only in case of very big fleets, where we are putting a dedicated commercial agreement in place to motivate them join committing to certain commercial pay outs. Otherwise, the admin burden is rather large to process such agreement with every fleet.
* for Ind Driver markets there is this legacy [Vehicle Branding T&Cs|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/driver-vehicle-branding-terms/]: it sets framework but falls short of setting exact payment amounts and leaves it to be unilaterally to be notified by Bolt
** in most cases branding bonus program is simply notified to fleets via e-mail with commercial conditions listed + linking to the above T&Cs.
** BUT this does not ensure Bolt’s commitment to keep this program running and gives Bolt all flexibility to  set fees and discontinue. And understand this would not work for PL.



Prob a way to go for PL would be to localise the [Vehicle Branding T&Cs|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/driver-vehicle-branding-terms/] so that it is tailored for PL fleet market. And publish them as PL dedicated Fleet Branding terms. However, these would still be general rules and would need to stop short of setting commercial terms (commission level; time commitment, etc.). But it would prob give comfort to Fleets that there is a contract, not just flex promise. We could also address their concerns about discontinuation by adding a 1-month (or so) notice period if we want to discontinue branding bonus pay-outs; as well as similar safeguards.



BUT -  these T&Cs would ultimately become THE terms for car branding for all fleets/drivers. AND this will require to set a flow on how we engage fleets into branding campaigns: 

(A) Do we communicate invitation to brand vehicles via e-mail and invite all fleets to join as long as they accept the branding T&Cs? We could communicate via e-mail / g-Form / etc.

(B) Do we want to make it open just for some fleets? do we want to have “specific” terms for different fleets?

It depends all on how wanna set this up operationally. I understand there are no “paper/dedicated” contracts with fleets in PL currently - so going old-school way where we attempt to sign a dedicated contract with each participating fleet would not make much sense. hi [~accountid:5f366e50d3796e0046f55683] , sending across some advice on the meals and sports portions respectively. 

_For example, the employer decides and states that the employees are entitled to a meal voucher of CZK 100 per day (shift worked)._

_In this case, on the side of the employee, CZK 82,60 per meal voucher represents tax free income. Remaining CZK 17,40 then represents taxable income, subject to social security, health insurance (both, employee’s as well as employer’s part) and tax, if the employer covers the full CZK 100. Many employers approach the situation in the way that they cover the tax fee amount, and the remainder is paid by the employee (deduction from the salary)._

_On the side of the company, as a tax-deductible cost can be treated 55% of the “contribution” for employees boarding, i.e. 55% of the value of the meal voucher, which is CZK 55. If the company pays for the full amount of the meal voucher, then CZK 45 is a non-deductible expense, if the company pays the full value of the meal voucher. If the company pays only the amount that is tax free for the employee, the amount of CZK 27,60 is a tax non-deductible expense._

And then for the sports expenses:

_With respect to the other benefits provided in accordance according to Section 6/9/d of the ITA, the condition for treating these benefits as tax free at the side of the employee is, that they are provided from tax non-deductible costs._ *_So, none of these benefits provided can be considered tax deductible for the company._* _In the case of the recreational purposes, the limitation applies to the tax fee amount at the side of the employee._ *_If the employee is provided with the recreational benefit higher than CZK 20,000, the amount exceeding this limit is considered taxable income, subject to social security, health insurance (both, employer’s and employee’s part) and wage tax._* _However, at the same time, it is still considered tax non-deductible for the company._

Hope this brings some clarity to the tax situation, but let me know if you need further guidance or details.

Here is the note from our external counsel. Please let me know if you would like to raise any follow up questions or if you would like the agreement to be reviewed? 

# *Pickers can work max 40 Hrs per week?*

This is the standard maximum workload for employees in Romania. It may be extended up to 48 hours, but this is qualified as overtime and (i) is subject to the consent of the employee, and (ii) must be compensated by equivalent of paid time off during the next 90 days, or by overtime payment. Overtime payment is subject to negotiation, but cannot be less than 75% of the basic salary.

*2. Must have max 5 days working, 2 days off?*

The 40 hours per week can be distributed unevenly, but, in this case, the schedule must be stipulated in the initial agreement (it can be done by reference to an Internal Regulation, but needs to be acknowledged by the employee beforehand). In any case no shift can exceed 12 hours. A daily 12 hours shift must be followed by a 24 hours break. Also, each working week should include a consecutive 48 hours break.

*3. We need to pay for 21 days even after they fire any pickers (I presume this is a commercial agreement we have with the employment agency, but would be helpful to know if there is anything under local law in relation to this, or whether this is fairly market standard)?* 

The only legal requirement in relation to the remuneration of the employment agency is that its commission should be included in the agreement with the beneficiary. Remuneration varies from one agency to another and is also based on the services they offer (e.g. price may vary if they have a roster of personnel they rotate, or if they need to recruit for certain positions based on client specifications).

However, in relation to your question, if the employment agency fires one of their employees, reasonably, the agency should replace them. This type of payment would be reasonable if Bolt would no longer need to fill in a position before the assignment period for the respective employee is over (unilateral termination without cause for an employee).

*4. 1 month salary as implementation fee (as above, again if you are able to comment whether this is market standard for employment agencies that would be helpful)?*

 The implementation fee is not legally regulated, but can be justified if the employment agency provides implementation services such as medical check-up, initial training, etc. (which are mandatory before taking on a new job, and are normally covered by the employer). However, it also depends if such fees are not already invoiced separately as cost by the employment agency. If you could provide the agreement for a quick review, we could indicate if it fairly market standard, all services considered.

*5. 24 hours gap/ rest between 2 shifts/ working days?*

A shift cannot exceed 12 hours. A daily 12 hours shift must be followed by a 24 hours break. Also, each working week should include a consecutive 48 hours break.

After the investigation with [Sinch dev team|https://sinchbolt.slack.com/archives/C012DHXP72M/p1652166003033629] we figured out that the bug is in Sinch SDK though there is a workaround that can be used in order to mitigate the issue on the current version of the SDK.

The bug affects only communication between Rider with Android 12 and Driver on any Platform (we tested only on Android, but should be the same for iOS Drivers)

The bug is in automatic audio routing that is used in the Rider app. Driver Android doesn’t suffer from this issue because in Driver they do not use this feature of Sinch SDK and they route audio themselves.

However there are two solutions for this problem:

# Wait until Sinch team releases a fix, so we could upgrade our SDK in Rider (Sinch team is aware of the issue and they probably start working on it soon).
# Get rid of automatic audio routing in Rider and implement it in a similar way as Driver did. 

Both solutions could be quite time consuming, but the second one we can manage better because there is no external dependency here.

* if possible - general description of reasoning of why information is requested, and how it pertains to investigation of the alleged crime - this is necessary for us to assess whether scope of requested data is proportionate and we won’t be disclosing more information that is needed for the purpose as prescribed under GDPR
* reference to applicable legal basis (e.g domestic Penal code) under which the police is making this specific request for the information, in particular if the purpose of the disclosure is confidential and we cannot assess the proportionality of the request.

Apologies for jumping in as I know this was addressed to Dougie , but he and I had a brief chat about this yesterday and as explained, it’s not the certification/accreditation that’s an issue. It's the actual compliance with ADR requirements since they are handling dangerous goods, as well as compliance with ISO 9001 requirements from a quality standpoint.

Clauses 3 and 4 read as follows and there really shouldn’t be any issues complying with these requirements if they are a professional 3PL - I’ve underlined the relevant provisions. They should explain if and why they are unable to comply with these. [~accountid:5e74c64ebea00d0c41188ee0]  feel free to add of course.

# *DANGEROUS GOODS*
## The Contractor +acknowledges that the E-vehicles run on ion lithium batteries which are classified as class 9 dangerous goods+ under the European Agreement concerning the International Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Road (the “*ADR*”). 
## The Contractor +shall obtain and maintain at its own expense all permits, licenses and documentation+ +*necessary*+ for compliance with Applicable Law and the ADR when providing the Services and will show proof of such compliance within one day upon Bolt’s request and allow Bolt or its representatives to audit the Contractor’s compliance. 
## The Contractor +undertakes to only use equipment (including but not limited to transporting vehicles and storage boxes) appropriate for handling E-vehicle ion lithium batteries+ in accordance with Applicable Law and the ADR when providing the Services.
## Contractor Personnel +must have completed at the expense of the Contractor so called ADR 1.3 training+ as per Section 1.3. of the ADR. The Contractor must keep the documentation of the completed training and provide proof of completed training within one day upon Bolt’s request. 
## The Contractor Personnel must at its own expense +participate in any mandatory training provided by Bolt+ or third party designated by Bolt for the handling, storage, and transportation of dangerous goods. 
## Annex 4 stipulates a non-exhaustive list with +minimum requirements that the Contractor shall abide by+ in regard to the E-vehicle ion lithium batteries.
# *CONTRACTOR WAREHOUSES*
## The Contractor shall +provide storage service in line with ISO 9001 quality standard+ to Bolt’s E-vehicle, equipment and other applicable assets in the contractor’s warehouse and provide access to such warehouses to Bolt as agreed in Annex 1 (the “*Contractor Warehouses*”).

# *_Please confirm that application of strike-through to the prior price is a compliant way of indicating price reduction in your jurisdiction. If not, please describe what is the compliant way of indicating price reduction in your jurisdiction._*

_As part of the Draft of the New Consumer Protection Act, the Slovak legislators adjust the price reduction mechanism in Section 7 as follows:_

_Section 7_

_Reduction of the price of goods_

_(1) The trader is obliged to state the prior price of the goods in each price reduction indication._

_(2) The prior price is the lowest price at which the trader sold or provided the goods_

_(a) less than 30 days before the price reduction; or_

_(b) from the beginning of the sale or supply of goods, if the trader sold or provided the goods less than 30 days before the price reduction._

_(3) In the event of a gradual reduction of the price, the trader may state the original price as the previous price before the first price reduction, regardless of the time of sale or provision of goods._

_The purpose of this provision is to prevent misleading price machinations by traders and thus misleading consumers about the amount of the real discount. The provision applies to all types of sales. However, it does not apply to various loyalty programs, vouchers and discount cards allowing consumers to claim a discount on all or part of the range of goods over a certain period of time/ at special dates (consumer’s birthdays) or discounts provided to loyalty program members. Where a trader states that a discount of, for example, 20% applies to all goods of one kind, it is sufficient for the prior price to be given only for a particular product and it is not necessary (or even possible) to state all original prices covered by such a statement. It does not matter how long the discount lasts. The prior price is always the price at which the trader provided the product during the period not less than 30 days before the price reduction._

 _This also applies to cases where the trader reduces the price for a short period and then increases it again, i.e. cases of sales events such as "Black Friday", even if there are several events like that in a row. In this case, the trader may also refer to the original price, but is also obliged to indicate the lowest price at which the product was provided at least 30 days before the price reduction. For example, a trader may state that at a 20% discount, the product costs € 80 instead of € 100 (the lowest price in the last 30 days) and also state that the original price or the price outside the sale is € 120. The exception is the gradual reduction of the price, when the trader must state only the original price, regardless of the period over which the goods are in sale. However, should such a gradual reduction take place over a very long period of time, the fairness of stating such an extensive period can still be assessed in terms of unfair commercial practices._

 

*_According to the Guidelines (Guidelines on the interpretation and application of Article 6a of Directive 98/6 / EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on consumer protection in the indication of the prices of products offered to consumers), a price reduction could be announced, for example: by indicating a new (lower) price together with an indication of the previous (higher) price. The previous price may be crossed out. E.g. "EUR 50 now, previously EUR 100" or "EUR 50 /_* *-_EUR 100"._-*

*_In the light of the above, we are of the opinion that when reducing the price of goods, it is sufficient to indicate the price reduction by crossing out the prior price._*

*_In the case of products and goods that have been on the market for less than 30 days (new goods), the trader should indicate the lowest price at which the product or goods had been sold._*

Hi Julia, 

it is not very straightforwardly explained in the Act. 

The law prescribes - in the case of Special forms of sale (Special forms of sale are considered to be the sale of products at prices lower than the prices in regular sales) the seller is obliged to indicate the price applied during the Special form of sale and the lowest price applied by the trader for the same service during the period of 30 days before the implementation of the special form of sale.

So, you are correct in case the special form of sale lasts continuously during a certain period of time. 

Meaning,  the following model is applied - -EUR 10- EUR 8, and if decreased further, then -EUR 10- EUR 6. 

However, if the special form of sale lasts for too long, the price is too long EUR 8 *_Please note that there are no specific rules on how long is too long i.e. how long the sale can last - the exception is seasonal sales_* then the question is what is considered as a regular price, EUR 10 or EUR 8? In this case, I suggest showing -EUR 8- EUR 6.

But if that will not be the case, then you are correct.

_Regarding your question on the possibility to terminate a lease agreement concluded for a definite period of time:_ *_the parties are free to specify in the contract the reasons for termination_*_. Therefore, if Bolt wants to provide in the contract the right to terminate for specific reasons (e.g. these reasons may be based on Bolt's experiences with previous warehouse leases), this should be agreed with the landlord and written in the contract._

 _However, if the parties do not specify the reasons for termination in the agreement, then the tenant can only terminate the agreement for the reasons described in the Civil Code. The basis for termination by the tenant is article 664 § 2 of the Civil Code, according to which if the leased item has defects which make it impossible to use for the intended purposes, and the landlord in spite of being notified about the defects failed to remove them in an appropriate time (or if the defects cannot be removed), the tenant may terminate the lease agreement. Referring to your question, I would like to emphasize that the Civil Code_ *_does not_* _specify what defects should be considered as those that make it impossible to use the leased item for the purposes intended by the parties - determination whether the reason for termination actually exists should be made individually._ *_For this reason, the best solution would be to specify in the contract the grounds upon which Bolt can terminate the contract_*_._

[@beatriz.leiva|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U02T9DPTUCD] have dedicated a lot of time over the last few months finding solutions for Rentals for the 3PL and the mechanics in *Belgium, Italy and now Spain*. Even though there is not a solution that fits all countries, please see *examples of what we have in BE and ES*:

* ES: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JBCi50WUtMxnkSt-tt3kqTLhBu6QbDTb/edit#|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JBCi50WUtMxnkSt-tt3kqTLhBu6QbDTb/edit#|smart-link]

I also highlight below a number of risks that you need to be aware of and that we'll specifically need to assess in light of FR law:

* *Employee lending risk:* In most of the West Eur countries, any direct instruction to the 3PL employees could lead to consider that there is an *unlawful assignment of employees from the 3PL to Bolt - which is often sanctioned by civil and criminal sanctions*. In some countries, it is possible to find a way around it  by having the 3PL designating a “Service Coordinator” who receive instructions from Bolt and then communicate them to the rest of the 3PL employees. In BE, it was also possible to add an instruction right clause, which sets out the limited 'instructions' Bolt can give to the 3PL employees.
* *Lease reclassification for use of warehouse:* The general rule should be that Bolt leases or sub-leases the warehouse directly and concludes a separate agreement for that purpose. The option of using 3PL's warehouse as a service should be used only in exceptional cases. From a legal perspective, the use of a warehouse could be considered as a lease relationship, this means that Bolt could be considered as a lessee and the 3PL as a lessor, and obligations arising from a traditional lease agreement could cause disputes.

Andrea, I’ve been trying to dig into Italy as a case with Fabio to understand their structures, unfortunately, our competitors seem to operate a very low transparency approach to how they have and what they have insured. In regards to the use of bikes, this might be a subject we can get Allianz to accommodating, in regards to scooters these are a very different subject especially in Italy.

Specifically for Italy, based on input we’ve received from external specialists in the field, scooters fall within the road traffic laws of Italy and thus have a unique strict liability for the owner where the drivers insurance fails; QED if for any reason our insurance on the rider fails, Bolt is automatically liable. To my reading this is what most of the cities have essentially put into the tenders in one form or another, but its important to note it also appears to be mirrored in the law.

In anycase, our challenge is to show either the councils that this is a manifestly bad idea because of the risk this user group pose to the public, or show Allianz that their perception of the risk is excessive and they indeed pose no greater risk to the performance of the insurance. Unfortunately there is a strong body of research from a multitude of fields that speak to the risk seeking nature of 13-18 y.o’s and not much that says they don’t or can’t cause injury to themselves and others when given the keys to a car.

I can happily assist in sourcing data that shows that 13-18 is a challenging demographic and that we as a responsible operator, with the general publics well being in mind, disagree with opening up a free floating service to this group.

Hey\! heres input from Andrei G. Please let me know if further questions arise.

In relation to the first question, indeed according to the Bolt Food T&Cs, the couriers are employees of each fleet which acts as an independent service provider, therefore no verification on Bolt's part is necessary. However, if the same couriers also act as ride-hailing drivers, as you know this activity is expressly regulated by GEO 49/2019 and the Bolt platform must ensure that all drivers are compliant with the legal obligations (i.e. the fact that they are at least 21 years old, they hold a valid driver's license at least 2 years old, they have the ARR certification as professional drivers, etc.).



As regards the second question, indeed a PFA may carry out the activities for which it is authorised, alone or together with a maximum of 3 persons, as an employer. However, any continuous professional activity must be carried out as an employee or a PFA, unless there is an express derogation (e.g. for company managers a mandate agreement may be concluded, without them being employees or PFAs). Therefore, a simple collaboration with an individual which is not project based, but would actually work regularly as a courier, is likely to be treated as a _de facto_ employment. The worst case entailed by this scenario is that, due to the absence of a clear regulation of the fleet's role in the food delivery business setup (unlike ride-hailing where drivers clearly "pertain" to the fleets, according to GEO 49/2019), there is a possibility that the individual is deemed by the authorities to be employed by Bolt and not by the fleet. Therefore, it is advisable that the individuals are employees of the fleet or PFAs themselves.

We have analysed the situation and the exchange of emails sent to us, and in the first place, it should be highlighted that the appointment of a local representative with address at Madeira, is not related with Madeira itself, but with the activity carried out by Bolt.

In fact, under Regional Decree n.º 14/2020/M (applicable to the activity of individual and remunerated transport of passengers in uncharacterised vehicles from an electronic platform – “*TVDE*”), in order to be granted the TVDE license to operate in the region, a local representative with address at Madeira needs to be appointed, if the service provider does not have its registered office at Madeira (which is the case). As such, this is not a specific requirement for any company to operate in Madeira, but a specific requirement for the TVDE activity at Madeira.

That being said, we believe that +*setting up a subsidiary in Madeira may reveal more burdensome*+ *than appointing the representative as before*. Setting up a company in Madeira *will entail incorporation and maintenance costs* (notably registration fees, accountants, social security costs for Directors, and others) *which may easily surpass the annual € 5,000 charged by the local representative* you appoint.

Please note that +*this representative is merely a local point of contact and he does not have access to any information or documents of Bolt*+. 

If the sole reason for which you are considering setting up a subsidiary at Madeira is the appointment of the representative, our opinion is that it is not worth it, and you can keep your current representative as the appointed representative for Bolt.

I did another round of analysis about the *did not deliver* orders and this time around i have a more concrete game (aka execution) plan.Based on my analysis we have roughly 7.5K order per week which were not delivered or where at the very least the courier did not switch order states correctly.
The criteria I used for detecting such orders was: {{distance_from_eater>=0.3km AND courier_ride_distance<1km}}So over the past 5 weeks (28.03-02.05) there were 37.5K orders like that. I also narrowed down the data set to couriers who had a significant amount of such orders (count of such orders in a week>=10 OR (count of such orders in a week>=3 AND ratio of such orders out of the total weekly orders>=33%)). After only looking at orders which were done by the remaining couriers the count of orders dropped down to 10821 or 2.16K per week. This tells us that majority of those undelivered orders are random and not carried out systematically by couriers.
In other words we are talking about 663 couriers over those 5 weeks or 133 couriers per week who have had significant amount of such orders and should either receive a temp block or at the very least be warned.I will list all the options on how we can handle this situation, they vary by effectiveness and development cost:

# Send out a in-app message or some other form of message after every such order
# Send out a in-app message or some other form of warning once courier reaches critical threshold of such orders
# Apply a scheduled block to a courier who reached a critical threshold of such orders
# Do 2. and 3. step + apply a hard block to the top bad couriers
# Label every such order and remove the courier earnings (in case of FP’s very bad UX, but is much more effective in killing courier earnings fraud)

My favorite solution:
Fraud builds a new checkpoint which will have the following actions available:

* Send out a in-app message warning the courier once he reaches critical threshold
* Apply a scheduled block of 1 day that doubles in duration after each previous block by the same rule

SQL used for analysis:

{code:sql}      WITH _weekly_total_orders AS (
      SELECT
      oc.courier_id,
      DATE_TRUNC('week',o.created) AS week,
      COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS count_of_orders_weekly
      FROM delivery.delivery_order_order AS o
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_provider AS op ON op.order_id=o.id AND op.provider_id=o.provider_id
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier AS oc ON oc.order_provider_id=op.id AND oc.state='delivered'
      WHERE o.state='delivered'
      AND o.created BETWEEN '2022-03-28' AND '2022-05-02'
      GROUP BY 1,2
      )
      SELECT
      o.country,
      o.id AS order_id,
      DATE_TRUNC('week',o.created) AS week,
      oc.courier_id,
      ROUND(distance_on_earth_km(pu.lat,pu.lng,del.lat,del.lng),2) AS courier_ride_distance,
      ROUND(LEAST(distance_on_earth_km(atc.lat,atc.lng,o.delivery_lat,o.delivery_lng),distance_on_earth_km(del.lat,del.lng,o.delivery_lat,o.delivery_lng)),2) AS distance_from_eater,
      ce.earning_amount/r.rate AS courier_earning,
      wto.count_of_orders_weekly
      FROM delivery.delivery_order_order AS o
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_provider AS op ON op.order_id=o.id AND op.provider_id=o.provider_id
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier AS oc ON oc.order_provider_id=op.id AND oc.state='delivered'
      LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates as r ON DATE(r.valid_on)=DATE(o.created) AND r.currency=o.currency
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS atp ON atp.city_id=o.city_id AND atp.order_id=o.id AND atp.order_courier_id=oc.id AND atp.to_state='arrived_to_provider'
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS pu ON pu.city_id=o.city_id AND pu.order_id=o.id AND pu.order_courier_id=oc.id AND pu.to_state='picked_up'
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS atc ON atc.city_id=o.city_id AND atc.order_id=o.id AND atc.order_courier_id=oc.id AND atc.to_state='arrived_to_client'
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log AS del ON del.city_id=o.city_id AND del.order_id=o.id AND del.order_courier_id=oc.id AND del.to_state='delivered'
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_earning AS ce ON ce.city_id=o.city_id AND ce.order_courier_id=oc.id
      LEFT JOIN _weekly_total_orders AS wto ON wto.courier_id=oc.courier_id AND wto.week=DATE_TRUNC('week',o.created)
      WHERE o.state='delivered'
      AND o.created BETWEEN '2022-03-28' AND '2022-05-02'
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
      HAVING distance_from_eater>=0.3 AND (courier_ride_distance<1 OR courier_ride_distance IS NULL){code}

* 400: Validation error. It means the request did not contain enough data points or in an invalid format and that ProcessOut cannot understand the API request.
* 404: The resource could not be found.
** This one will happen in multiple cases where you are trying to either leverage or fetch a resource that does not exist.
** Ex: Requesting a authorization with a card ID or invoice ID that can’t be found.
* 409: This one is used for conflicts. For example when you try to do an authorisation, it hasn't yet finished and you try another action or the same it will return that.
* 410: This one would be any generic error (i.e. invalid API keys, errors coming from the PSP/APM etc..)

{noformat}mysql> explain
    -> select * from 
    -> (
    ->     SELECT id FROM `chat` chat
    ->     WHERE chat.created < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
    ->     ORDER BY id LIMIT 100
    -> ) old_chats
    -> JOIN `chat_order` co ON old_chats.id = co.chat_id
    -> JOIN `chat_participant` cp ON old_chats.id = cp.chat_id
    -> JOIN `event` e ON old_chats.id = e.chat_id
    -> ;
+----+-------------+------------+------------+--------+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+---------+--------------+------+----------+------------------------------------------+
| id | select_type | table      | partitions | type   | possible_keys                     | key                               | key_len | ref          | rows | filtered | Extra                                    |
+----+-------------+------------+------------+--------+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+---------+--------------+------+----------+------------------------------------------+
|  1 | PRIMARY     | <derived2> | NULL       | ALL    | NULL                              | NULL                              | NULL    | NULL         |  100 |   100.00 | NULL                                     |
|  1 | PRIMARY     | co         | NULL       | eq_ref | chat_id_IDX                       | chat_id_IDX                       | 4       | old_chats.id |    1 |   100.00 | NULL                                     |
|  1 | PRIMARY     | cp         | NULL       | ref    | chat_id_participant_id_UNIQUE_IDX | chat_id_participant_id_UNIQUE_IDX | 4       | old_chats.id |    2 |   100.00 | NULL                                     |

Hi Julia, 

The answers for Croatia are below, waiting for answers for CZ and unfortunately, Slovakia is again a problem - they can send their answers on Monday. 😞 

+*Croatia*+

# *end date of the campaign - is it a must to mention the end date for the discount?* 

No specific rules regarding the duration of the campaign. However, as in other countries, a very long period of duration can be considered misleading. 

Furthermore, as discussed before - there is a rule that the seller is obliged to indicate the price applied during the Special form of sale and the lowest price applied by the trader for the same service during the period of 30 days before the implementation of the special form of sale.

In case a certain discount is offered for a very long period of time it could be considered that discounted price is the regular one. 

*2. exclusions - do we need to state all the products that are excluded from the campaign or there can be one generic legal phrase, like "some products might be excluded from discount" that will work in all markets?*

The misleading campaign is forbidden, so it is recommended to mention which products are excluded at least the type of product e.g. “_all alcohol and tobacco products are excluded”_

*3. push notifications - these are really short, do we need to mention all the details also in push message, e.g. the dates and the excluded products?*

The misleading campaign is forbidden, so it is recommended to mention which products are excluded at least the type of product e.g. “_all alcohol and tobacco products are excluded”_

Hi Anthony,

Thanks for submitting the document for review. Below are my comments. Let me know if you have any questions.

# *Confidentiality:* Have we already shared confidential information for Steer to prepare the proposal? If so, have we signed an NDA? The Terms and Conditions (Ts&Cs) are only effective from the start of the services, and so are the confidentiality obligations. Thus, if we have already shared confidential information and not signed an NDA, we should request Steer to change the Ts&Cs so that the confidentiality obligations also cover confidential information disclosed during/for the proposal preparation.
# *Sharing/disclosing the study:* Clause 3.7 Ts&Cs prevents Bolt from disclosing the study to third parties unless Steer agrees to it in writing (sharing with Affiliates and professional advisors is permitted). Item 5.7 of the proposal also restricts publishing the study for a public audience. If we intend to use/share the study externally, we should explain our needs to Steer and ask them to include express authorisation for it in the Ts&Cs.
# *Out-of-pocket expenses:* Do we expect Steer to incur significant out-of-pocket expenses, such as traveling expenses? Clause 8.4 Ts&Cs requires Bolt to reimburse all reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by Steer. I suggest that we include a threshold above which Bolt’s prior approval must be obtained (e.g., out-of-pocket expenses exceeding GBP 80).
# *Taxes:* Bolt may not deduct or withhold any taxes from payments made under the agreement (clause 8.5 Ts&Cs). Even if this is required by law, Bolt shall gross-up the taxes and assume the costs, so that Steer receives the agreed price in full.
# *Limitation of liability:* In item A.1 Ts&Cs it is said that Steer will prepare an additional clause regarding liability. Have we already seen it? In principle, I don’t see an issue in limiting Steer’s liability to 100% of their fees (instead of 100% + GBP 100K as it stands right now) as they are only providing consulting services and we cannot hold them accountable for any actions we take based on their advice anyway. However, let’s ask Steer to make the limitation mutual (clause 11.1).
# *Non-solicitation:* Let’s also ask Steer to make clause 13 Ts&Cs mutual.
# *Bolt’s policies:* Please ask Steer to include a provision whereby they commit to comply with Bolt’s brand guidelines and information security policies. Wording suggestion: “The Company shall comply, and ensure its employees, agents and subcontractors also comply, with the Client’s Brand Guidelines ([https://bolt.eu/en/brand/guidelines/|https://bolt.eu/en/brand/guidelines/|smart-link] ) and Information Security Code of Practice ([https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/|https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/|smart-link] ).”

Best,

Thiago

*Estonia*

In the case of a discount, the final price of the goods means the new reduced price. The discount must be calculated on the basis of the same price at which the goods were previously sold by the firm and must not be artificially inflated before the discount begins.

The level of the discount and the fact that all goods are offered at a lower price must be made clear and unambiguous to the consumer at the point of sale before the transaction is concluded.

*It is misleading for the consumer to advertise a large discount when in fact only a small proportion of the goods on sale are actually on sale.*

When advertising the percentage range of the discount, you should take into account that the discounted goods must include a proportion of the goods with the lowest and the highest percentage discount. In doing so, it should be borne in mind that the consumer's transaction decision is primarily influenced by the upper end of the range, i.e. the maximum percentage discount allowed.

The use of the terms "all" and "all" in the context of the information on the sale at a reduced price should be seen as conveying the message to the consumer that the full range of goods on offer is on sale at a reduced price. *Various exclusions (e.g.: excluding discounted products; a particular product group; a particular brand; new season goods) are generally not recommended*. When designing an advertising message, the visual interaction (text/image/sound/letter size/colour scheme/lettering distinctiveness, etc.) and the resulting association in the mind of the advertiser must be taken into account.

*Misrepresentation of the price, the basis on which it is calculated or the existence of a price advantage, and the misleading use of the terms 'all' and 'all' when advertising the sale of goods on preferential terms, constitute misleading commercial practices* within the meaning of the Consumer Protection Act. In the case of loyalty promotions, you should ensure that the special price for loyalty customers is not visually dominant when you make price disclosures. The consumer must also be able to see the price of the goods applicable to the regular customer by paying average attention.

The words 'final sale', 'clearance sale', 'clearance sale' or any other words or expressions having the same meaning may be used in the context of a promotional offer only if the conditions set out below are fulfilled at the same time:

the sale relates to the final sale of all or a limited part of the goods sold;
such a sale lasts for a limited period;
the price of the goods so sold is significantly lower than the normal price.


Words such as 'sale', 'discount' or other words or expressions having the same meaning may be used in the context of a notification of a sale of goods on preferential terms only where the conditions set out below coexist:

* *the sale relates to goods normally sold by the trader;*
* *such a sale lasts for a limited period;*
* *the price of the goods so sold is significantly lower than the normal price.*


If you intend to offer and sell goods at a price lower than the published selling and unit price, the publication of a new reduced selling and unit price *is not necessary only if a uniform discount applies at the point of sale for a short period and such discount applies to all goods in the shop without any exceptions or exclusions.* In such a situation, it would be unreasonable to require all goods to be re-priced for a short period.

Good and valuable discussion on repeating dilemma (where to produce template / T&C) 👍 

Please allow to add some thoughts from me re: "decision tree" to be considered in similar situations.

First of all we should recognize that *NO* "templating" can be resolved in the silence of cabinet by the lawyer alone - it requires stakeholder involvement _(sometimes more/sometimes less, but certainly the need is there, especially when it comes to commercial conditions or frame of template/T&C)_. 

I agree that there is a good case for *"starting templating on HQ-layer"*, if underlying activity occurs repeatedly in multiple countries *AND* HQ-stakeholder _(in present case HQ Marketing)_ agrees to take the matter into their agenda and correspondingly requests production _(with its own proper involvement)_ from their Legal Counsel _(in present case Marja-Liisa)_.

However, situation *is different if this condition is not met.* If HQ Marketing sees the matter as low priority *OR* finds that it should be left for local marketing teams simply because out of trust _(local teams know best how to maximize our GMV with given category of marketing activity)_ and have therefore zero appetite to regulate/restrict local stars. We have in this case interested business stakeholder(s) (Local Marketing teams) *on local layer*, *NOT* @ HQ.

In this case it is *local business stakeholder(s)* who should contribute with their respective input to their respective Legal Counsel(s), who should help them with in-country implementation of local marketing activity in question.

*I categorically refuse to* agree that production of template/T&C on *local layer* has to result in what you Kaija describe as _"every field team member starts to create its own terms and conditions then I believe we are not using our legal team (human) resource in a proper and wise way"_. 

*Nothing stops GFT to leverage on templates/T&C already produced by one GFT member so that similar effect of efficiency is achieved* *_(we make first investment and then re-use it regionally or globally to save resources)_**.*

Needless to say that you are always welcome to reach out for expert input from subject matter experts (IP) or HQ Counsels from HQ Legal when working "on local templating layer" - we are here for you whenever bandwith situation and client priorities of HQ layer so permit.

*Romania:*

First, we assume the blanket discount does not generate selling under acquisition cost, as this type of campaign is subject to additional rules which we have touched in the past with Edi.

The concept of blanket discount is not expressly regulated, but retailers are generally allowed to reduce prices (subject to staying above acquisition cost), as long as the discount is not misleading.

In order for the discount not to be misleading, Government Ordinance 99/2000 on the retail of products and services sets the following rules:

(i) it must state the products and whether re-stocks will be available or the discount is subject to the current available stock;

(ii) it must clearly identify the original price and the new price (or the discount percentage), so that the consumer can compute the actual discount;

(iii) the original price must be the average price of the previous 30 days before the campaign. 

In light of the above:

(i) the end of the campaign is not necessary to be provided, however Bolt needs to assess whether it will assume the obligation to re-stock the products as long as the discount announcement is on. Another way to proceed is to announce that the discount is applicable to the extent of the existing stock.

(ii) exclusions - since Bolt needs to make available the discount computation for each product, it will be clear when the consumer actually accesses the app what products are subject to the discount. However, Bolt needs to make sure that the overall announcement is not misleading, in a way that the consumer expects all products are on sale. A general phrase would work, the one customarily used is that the discount applies to selected products, but phrasing it by means of exclusion could work, as well.

(iii) push notifications - these can provide just the range of the discount (in percentages) and that the discount applies to a selection of products/that some products are excluded.

Best, 

Liisa

+*Update - Further advice received from DLA (12 May):*+

* +What is exactly the role of the appointed local representative? Is it just like a 'postbox service'? Or do they have rights and obligations?+

{color:#4c9aff}DLA Piper PT: the law does not determine the exact role of the representative. Please note that the request to appoint a local representative has been referred to the Constitutional Court to determine its compatibility with the EU law. The Constitutional Court determined the validity of this appointment for non-resident entities operating in Madeira. {color}{color:#4c9aff}*This is due essentially with tax reasons* {color}{color:#4c9aff}and with determining the existence of a permanent establishment in Madeira. Because the TVDE activity is carried out on movable means (cars), the appointment of a local representative serves as the indication of an existing fixed/permanent establishment at Madeira, so as to legitimize the collection of Corporate Income Tax related with income obtained in Madeira – subject to different rules and tax rates as the ones in Continental Portugal.{color}

→ [~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c] [~accountid:610a3ee7ae72b2006f5fb907] copying you here FYI as this relates to tax 😉 Let me know if we need to discuss anything (if that’s the case, please put some time in my diary the w/c 23rd may as i’m attending the Legal Summit in Tallinn all of next week - thanks\!)

* +Are they meant to receive any formal communication addressed to Bolt and related to our operations in Madeira?+

{color:#4c9aff}DLA Piper PT: as mentioned above, {color}{color:#4c9aff}*the law does not impose any obligations on this representative, neither the obligation to receive notifications*{color}{color:#4c9aff}. As such, we understand {color}{color:#4c9aff}*this is a mere point of contact*{color}{color:#4c9aff}, similar to the tax representative one needs to appoint to request a non-resident tax number in Portugal. These tax representatives have no tax liability before the Tax Authorities (there are no legal grounds to do so) and serve merely as a point of contact and notifications with the represented entity.{color}

* +Could the appointed local representative have any kind of liability if something happens? any responsibility as to our operations?+

{color:#4c9aff}DLA Piper: there are no legal grounds to do so. For a local representative to have any operational or tax liabilities, this had to be expressly foreseen in the law, which is not. Throughout the Regional Decree n.º 14/2020/M (TVDE activities in Madeira) the only reference to the representative is on the article imposing its appointment. {color}{color:#4c9aff}*There are no further obligations or liabilities imposed* {color}{color:#4c9aff}by this piece of legislation.{color}

If you think it would be helpful, we can enter in contact with DRETT (entity responsible for TVDE operations at Madeira), to know their understanding as to the exact role of this representative.

Dear [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] , please find below the answer for CZ. 

+*Czech Republic*+

# *End date of the campaign*

The law does not explicitly state the obligation to state in your advertising messages the date until which a certain discount action applies. However, you are bound by the general conditions for communicating the prices of goods to the consumer - your message should be as clear and comprehensible as possible. If a particular discount will only be provided for a limited time, then it is certainly appropriate to inform the consumer of this fact. CTI warned me that if you do not specify the end date of a particular discount, you run the risk that your customers will request this discount after the discount action ended and you will have to comply. 

I understand that you do not always have enough space to include all the details of the discount action in your marketing communication, but by communicating this information you are actually covering yourself, so it is in your best interest to communicate it to consumers. It may not be necessary, for example, in brief push notifications, but, for example, after clicking on notification, the conditions of the discount promotion should be obvious (what goods are concerned, for how long the discount is valid, etc.).

2. *Exclusions*

In Czech marketing, the phrase that the discount applies to "selected goods" is usually used, which means that only chosen products are discounted (not all of your products). Thus, promotional emails may state that it provides a discount on "selected items", which actually means that some products may be excluded from the discount. But again, you must comply with the law's requirements for the certainty and comprehensibility of the information provided to consumers. It should therefore be clear which specific products are covered by the discount and which products are excluded from the discount. Therefore, for each product included in the discount promotion, the final price for the consumer should be indicated and, if applicable, information whether or not it is affected by the discount promotion - in this way it will be clear to the consumer that the discount applies to specific product (or not).

*3. Push notifications*

As stated before - the CTI stated that such brief reports does not have to necessarily contain all the information. However, they must not be misleading, they must be true and the necessary information should be communicated to the customer in another comprehensible way. E.g. in the case of a brief notification, the customer should obtain all the necessary information after clicking on the notification - or in another understandable and non-burdensome way. 

Keep in mind that the price after the discount must be expressed by a specific amount, which is final for the customer and which he will pay you. It is not possible to indicate the final price in the form of a percentage discount from the original amount. The specific amount (after discount) that will be charged must always be stated. Therefore, it is not possible to say that you apply a general discount to selected goods and then let the customer to deduct this discount from the original price. For each discounted product, the final price including the discount must be stated so that the customer knows exactly how much he will pay for the goods.

The original amount (before discount) does not have to be stated. However, CTI also can check whether the discount was actually provided (i.e. whether the price you provide as discounted really includes the discount). So if you only mention the discounted price, be prepared to prove that the discount really happened. Therefore, you are not required to display the original price before the discount, however, this may be useful for marketing reasons. 

A model example of your procedure is as follows: Users of your application will receive a brief notification in mobile phones that you are providing a X% discount on selected goods for a limited period of time. After clicking on the notification, the customer finds out the period when the discount promotion is valid, what goods are concerned and other details. After opening your application and displaying the goods that fall into the discount promotion, your customer will see the discounted goods with the final price they will pay for the goods after the application of discount.

If you need any further information let me know. CTI was helpful in this matter, so if you need to make sure that your planned marketing action is compliant with local law, we can send them a draft of this marketing action and ask CTI, whether CTI considers this action legal or not.”

BR, 

Iva

For device identifier we are using {{identifierForVendor}} value ([https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uidevice/1620059-identifierforvendor|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uidevice/1620059-identifierforvendor]). This value is provided by iOS (and we also “cache” this value in device keychain). In the doc it is stated, that:

{quote}If the value is {{nil}}, wait and get the value again later. This happens, for example, after the device has been restarted but before the user has unlocked the device.{quote}

So far this is the only suspect for the problem.



There are two cases-candidates that could cause such behavior:

* Background Fetch support in Live builds of the app (iOS could launch the app into the background state after device has been rebooted, but was not unlocked yet), and
* silent push notification (such notification can arrive after device has been rebooted, but was not unlocked yet)

But real device is needed to check if that is the case.

+*Czech Republic*+

# *End date of the campaign*

The law does not explicitly state the obligation to state in your advertising messages the date until which a certain discount action applies. However, you are bound by the general conditions for communicating the prices of goods to the consumer - your message should be as clear and comprehensible as possible. If a particular discount will only be provided for a limited time, then it is certainly appropriate to inform the consumer of this fact. CTI warned me that if you do not specify the end date of a particular discount, you run the risk that your customers will request this discount after the discount action ended and you will have to comply. 

I understand that you do not always have enough space to include all the details of the discount action in your marketing communication, but by communicating this information you are actually covering yourself, so it is in your best interest to communicate it to consumers. It may not be necessary, for example, in brief push notifications, but, for example, after clicking on notification, the conditions of the discount promotion should be obvious (what goods are concerned, for how long the discount is valid, etc.).

*2. Exclusions*

In Czech marketing, the phrase that the discount applies to "selected goods" is usually used, which means that only chosen products are discounted (not all of your products). Thus, promotional emails may state that it provides a discount on "selected items", which actually means that some products may be excluded from the discount. But again, you must comply with the law's requirements for the certainty and comprehensibility of the information provided to consumers. It should therefore be clear which specific products are covered by the discount and which products are excluded from the discount. Therefore, for each product included in the discount promotion, the final price for the consumer should be indicated and, if applicable, information whether or not it is affected by the discount promotion - in this way it will be clear to the consumer that the discount applies to specific product (or not).

*3. Push notifications*

As stated before - the CTI stated that such brief reports does not have to necessarily contain all the information. However, they must not be misleading, they must be true and the necessary information should be communicated to the customer in another comprehensible way. E.g. in the case of a brief notification, the customer should obtain all the necessary information after clicking on the notification - or in another understandable and non-burdensome way. 

Keep in mind that the price after the discount must be expressed by a specific amount, which is final for the customer and which he will pay you. It is not possible to indicate the final price in the form of a percentage discount from the original amount. The specific amount (after discount) that will be charged must always be stated. Therefore, it is not possible to say that you apply a general discount to selected goods and then let the customer to deduct this discount from the original price. For each discounted product, the final price including the discount must be stated so that the customer knows exactly how much he will pay for the goods.

The original amount (before discount) does not have to be stated. However, CTI also can check whether the discount was actually provided (i.e. whether the price you provide as discounted really includes the discount). So if you only mention the discounted price, be prepared to prove that the discount really happened. Therefore, you are not required to display the original price before the discount, however, this may be useful for marketing reasons. 

A model example of your procedure is as follows: Users of your application will receive a brief notification in mobile phones that you are providing a X% discount on selected goods for a limited period of time. After clicking on the notification, the customer finds out the period when the discount promotion is valid, what goods are concerned and other details. After opening your application and displaying the goods that fall into the discount promotion, your customer will see the discounted goods with the final price they will pay for the goods after the application of discount.

If you need any further information let me know. CTI was helpful in this matter, so if you need to make sure that your planned marketing action is compliant with local law, we can send them a draft of this marketing action and ask CTI, whether CTI considers this action legal or not.”

Hi [~accountid:5d7b6987656e2a0dbab30492], thanks for the feedback\! I just have a few comments/questions. 

First, rate limiting on IP may not be helpful where the attacker can simply automate changing of IPs (this was done to achieve this report). And for other forms of IP blocks, we could end up spending resources on maintaining this static block list if blocking is not automated.

Secondly, the issue here is in the fraud rule that triggers when a person provides incorrect SMS codes for a phone number leading to the phone number being blocked. This can simply be abused to lock out real and potential customers from using Bolt (maybe indefinitely?).
As this means an improvement of the fraud rule logic to account for this possible abuse, I agree that monitoring will help to recognise this activity. But I wanted to find out why monitoring is the preferred course of action over actual updates to the fraud rule to “fix” the issue (eg release blocking of phone numbers after some time?). 

Lastly, the analyst reported that they were blocked for several days. How long do the phone numbers that trigger this fraud action actually stay blocked?

 [https://www.app.invoicexpress.com/documents/1006162638e043ce38ce072ad3550134b70e3d1099d258d5d|https://www.app.invoicexpress.com/documents/1006162638e043ce38ce072ad3550134b70e3d1099d258d5d|smart-link]

Generally, VAT only applies where there is both a supply and consideration given. Therefore, if there is no specific charge for service, but the customer pays a tip anyway (i.e., +the tip is voluntary+), the tip is outside the scope of VAT (i.e., no supply of service / not part of the consideration for the supply of delivery service). If the tip is not voluntary, then it becomes within the scope of VAT (but this is not how our tipping feature should work as I understand).

Any such voluntary tips are not within the scope of VAT regardless of whether:

* the amount appears on the invoice;
* payment is made by cheque, cash or credit/debit card;
* the amount is passed on to employees (e.g. where couriers are employed by Bolt or agency services are used).
* The above applies regardless of the courier (or the fleet) being VAT-registered or non-VAT registered. 
* Where the courier services are provided by a fleet, even where the fleet retains part of the tips received as its commission, the total amount of the tip remains outside the scope of VAT. 

Hope this clarifies\!

When drivers apply via the portal as they always should, they are only assigned per default to the regular categories e.g. Bolt, Economy etc.

*1.End date of the campaign* 

Generally, the seller/advertiser is not obliged to mention the end date for a discount/campaign. The Slovak law does not impose any special restrictions or obligations in this regard and not mentioning of the end date is not directly punishable from the competent state authorities.

Of course, a very-long-lasting campaigns, especially in comparison with the period during which the products is sold at at non-discounted price, can be considered as an unfair commercial practice and/or misleading claim under the The Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council), as well as the Slovak Customer Protection Act. This though applies regardless from whether the campaign’s end date is mentioned in the add or not.

*2. Exclusions*

 The Slovak law does not require to provide the customer with an exact list of the products excluded from the campaign. It is though indeed necessary to clearly indicate to the customer that the discount is not applicable to the entire menu/ all products of a particular seller, as otherwise this might be considered as a misleading commercial practice and as a direct breach of the Customer Protection Act, punishable by a fine up to EUR 166,000.

The law does not set any special requirement to the wording of the exclusion notice. Therefore, we opine that the wording "_some products might be excluded from discount_" (or similar) is appropriate for the use in this case.

*3. Push notifications*

There is no specific regulation as to the push notifications. As the end date and the list of excluded products do not need to be mentioned in the advertisement/campaign itself, it is not necessary to present these in the push notifications either. We though recommend to indicate that some products might be excluded from the discount in the push notification as well, or at least refer the customer to such information presented in the app itself. Without the exclusion notice, this could be again considered as a misleading commercial practice in regard to a product’s price indication.

2. The above mentioned phrase should be sufficient.

+*Slovakia*+

*1.End date of the campaign* 

Generally, the seller/advertiser is not obliged to mention the end date for a discount/campaign. The Slovak law does not impose any special restrictions or obligations in this regard and not mentioning of the end date is not directly punishable from the competent state authorities.

Of course, a very-long-lasting campaigns, especially in comparison with the period during which the products is sold at at non-discounted price, can be considered as an unfair commercial practice and/or misleading claim under the The Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council), as well as the Slovak Customer Protection Act. This though applies regardless from whether the campaign’s end date is mentioned in the add or not.

*2. Exclusions*

 The Slovak law does not require to provide the customer with an exact list of the products excluded from the campaign. It is though indeed necessary to clearly indicate to the customer that the discount is not applicable to the entire menu/ all products of a particular seller, as otherwise this might be considered as a misleading commercial practice and as a direct breach of the Customer Protection Act, punishable by a fine up to EUR 166,000.

The law does not set any special requirement to the wording of the exclusion notice. Therefore, we opine that the wording "_some products might be excluded from discount_" (or similar) is appropriate for the use in this case.

*3. Push notifications*

There is no specific regulation as to the push notifications. As the end date and the list of excluded products do not need to be mentioned in the advertisement/campaign itself, it is not necessary to present these in the push notifications either. We though recommend to indicate that some products might be excluded from the discount in the push notification as well, or at least refer the customer to such information presented in the app itself. Without the exclusion notice, this could be again considered as a misleading commercial practice in regard to a product’s price indication.

The Risk and Safety team's Demerit Decay system is built on the fact that the users get blocked for an X amount of time as specified in the [Blocking Matrix|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nHHagVR4R6KIHJunaK62GWHqda-nKnweMo3kkPOryic/edit#gid=1122088492] based on the Risk Type, whether the event is Confirmed or not (do we have evidence) and Occurrence (number of previous reports together with the current one for the reported user).

*How to take previous safety reports into account (Demerit Decay)?*

Demerit Decay means that *older safety events should not be held against a user when considering their previous offences and consequential actions.* Safety events expire after a certain amount of time depending on the Risk Type if the user has not committed any more misconduct.

* For *regular events*, it's 3 months. When checking for previous offences, only take into account offences that took place within the last 3 months. 
* For *significant/unique events*, it's 1 year. When checking for previous offences, only take into account offences that took place within the last year.

Hi [~accountid:5d773c785a4d810d2c4de81c] , I am sorry the table is queried slower than expected. Yes, it is external table, stored as files on S3 and queried using Redshift Spectrum layer. I see it has some issues, but it is due to technical limitations (e.g. it is partitioned hourly, where it could be easily partitioned even in year/month schema. But our ingestion limitations require partitioning to be coupled to ingestion frequency. Theoretically we could move it, but we do such only for tables which are base for frequently used dashboards of frequently calculated ETLs. If you would like to query the data more frequently, you could also implement an ETL to have pre-aggregated data in Redshift table for fast queries. 

Also be aware how you query it. For instance LIMIT is not pushed down to Spectrum. When you see the plan you notice it is not in Spectrum. 

{noformat}XN Limit  (cost=0.00..151.83 rows=100 width=3644)
  ->  XN Partition Loop  (cost=0.00..50584162512.50 rows=33316500000 width=3644)
        ->  XN Seq Scan PartitionInfo of ext_rental.mds_events  (cost=0.00..12.50 rows=334 width=8)
              Filter: (created_date > '2022-05-10'::date)
        ->  XN S3 Query Scan mds_events  (cost=0.00..150997500.00 rows=99750000 width=3636)
"              ->  S3 Seq Scan ext_rental.mds_events location:""s3://taxify-immutable-data-converted/live/cdc_mysql/rental/mds_events"" format:PARQUET  (cost=0.00..150000000.00 rows=99750000 width=3636)"
                    Filter: (((event_type)::text = 'vehicle_hidden_due_charge'::text) OR ((event_type)::text = 'vehicle_hidden_due_maintenance'::text))
{noformat}

Other anti-patter for Spectrum queries is using {{SELECT * ...}}.

Also when you execute 

{noformat}select count(1) from ext_rental.mds_events where created_date ='2022-05-10'
                                             and event_type in ('vehicle_hidden_due_charge','vehicle_hidden_due_maintenance');{noformat}

you see you get 29073 rows.

Then querying e.g. (just a single partition, and columns specified)

{noformat}select
       e.charge, e.event_data, e.event_type, e.lat, e.lng, e.vehicle_id
from ext_rental.mds_events as e
where e.created_date ='2022-05-10'and e.created_hour = 12
  and e.event_type in ('vehicle_hidden_due_charge','vehicle_hidden_due_maintenance')
limit 100;{noformat}

Will be more efficient and enough for exploration.

(Please be aware that a lot of query execution time is actually queue time, when RS is at load.).

** _chargeback_payments:_ the amount of chargebacks exceeds the amount we allow. You can mention to the user that they’ve had multiple chargebacks due to which we can’t delete their account.
