First of all let’s define what’s a late invoice: 
*Late Invoice* - an invoice which is received by the client a day or more later than the expected date. It has nothing to do with the invoice generation as the entry is created into the backend on time & generally speaking then the invoice is generated. Here’s when the invoices are generated - 2nd each month + for April we had an incident where we had to regenerate the invoices:

!Screenshot 2022-05-19 at 12.37.15.png|width=1112,height=540!

It’s just a row in our tables which means it doesn’t become a physical thing before the email (containing a link) is sent to the client. So late invoice is defined by the date when we are sending the email. Here’s the graph showing when are we sending the emails containing the invoice:

!Screenshot 2022-05-19 at 12.39.50.png|width=1118,height=540!

h3. *Driver Monthly Invoices*

Each month we generate an aggregate invoice for drivers & share it via email. It shows driver’s commission & balance at the end of the period. For the average driver this document doesn’t matter as they are keeping their balance positive hence there’s no further input needed from them (i.e. they don’t have to make any manual payments to Bolt separately). 
For this analysis I’ve included only these invoices which require driver’s input meaning the invoice contains instructions to pay & how much they will have to pay. Unfortunately we don’t store driver’s balance in the backend for a specific day (the number for the invoice is created on a fly with no records) so as a workaround I’ve used {{invoicing_client_current_balance_log}} table in RS which doesn’t give us 100% accurate results (as the snapshot is taken once per day) but could be used to estimate roughly how many drivers balance is negative by the end of the month.

In 2022 (Jan - April) we’ve generated ~750k of such invoices from which ~620k (83%) were sent a day or more late than the ‘expected’ date. The email delay is specified on invoice issuer level & usually it’s between 1 - 3 days (meaning the emails are queued for sending 1 - 3 days later than the entry is created in our backend). This is due to limited resources when trying to send so many invoices all at once hence it takes time to process all the requests. Top 5 markets affected are:

|country|late_invoices|count|late %|
|ng|195308|206166|94.73%|
|sa|89413|99557|89.81%|
|gh|62913|96910|64.92%|
|za|63536|90727|70.03%|
|az|65447|76736|85.29%|


But as we can see vast majority of these invoices are sent late - what’s the impact of these invoices which were sent late? & what if we would improve our email sending quality such that more emails would be sent on time? Also what’s the difference between driver & company based drivers (as responsibility for debt is different between those)? 

Firstly, let check if the email has any impact on driver’s balance - if a driver’s balance is negative on the invoice issued date does it matter when they receive an invoice & if the balance is positive on the due date? Or have they cleared their debt when they’ve received the invoice? 

From 2022 data, we don’t see much effect when the email is sent:

* If the invoice is shared on-time: 27% of drivers have cleared their debt by the due date
* If the invoice is shared late: 30% of drivers have cleared their debt by the due date

For driver-based drivers (= drivers are responsible for their negative balance) we see 26% of drivers have cleared their debt when receiving the email late & 24% when they receive the email on-time
For company-based drivers (= FOs are responsible for driver’s negative balance) we see 31% drivers cleared their debt when receiving the email late & 35% when they receive the email on-time. The number of drivers using company-based logic is very small vs driver-based & in general FOs are responsible for driver’s balance (meaning less drivers are in debt overall).

Next, let’s check the driver payments (manual + inapp + cellulant) before & after they receive the email with the invoice:
As we can see if the invoice is sent on-time drivers are actively making payments after the email was received - we see an increase of 20% in payments 6 days after the email has been sent which contribute ~8% of monthly GMV.

!Screenshot 2022-05-19 at 13.29.11.png|width=50%!

^X-axis = difference between the payment & when the email was sent (in days).^
^Y-axis = sum of payments per day in EUR.^

Looking at the same graph but for drivers who’ve received their invoice late completely different picture appears. We see drivers are actually making payments in advance i.e. before they receive the email containing the invoice. We see 16% increase in payments 5 days before they receive their email which contributes ~6% of monthly GMV. Meaning a lot of drivers doesn’t care about the invoice - they are making payments in the beginning of the month just because their balance is negative & they would like to get a payout. 

!Screenshot 2022-05-19 at 13.29.23.png|width=481,height=299!

But we do see a slight uptick in payments for 3 days after the invoice email is shared (late). These are the drivers who want to pay per invoice & waiting for the document. For that period we see 3% increase in payments which contribute 1% of monthly GMV. Meaning the 1% of GMV we could’ve gained earlier if we would’ve sent the invoice earlier/on-time. Now the question arises - what if they’ve paid earlier? Are they getting blocked because drivers are waiting for their invoice? On a large scale the impact is negligible as vast majority of these payments are from in-app. Which comes to Cellulant we don’t see any increase in payments after the driver received their invoice. For manual payments there’s a jump of 0.5% after the email is received which means ~40k drivers are waiting for the invoice before they are making a manual payment. During this time they could get cash-blocked or stop driving (= loss in GMV) but this would require further analysis (as in the same time they could make inapp/Cellulant payments & keep driving). So for now we can say the impact is small compared to the total. 

But what about other possible areas could be affected? Well the easiest is to check our CS tickets regarding drivers complaining about the invoice. We can see a correlation between when the invoices are being sent & when drivers are opening a CS ticket:

!Screenshot 2022-05-19 at 14.24.22.png|width=1115,height=539!

~50% increase in CS tickets during the days when the invoices are being sent. This comes up to ~200 more tickets per month related to issues with the invoice (or ~500 EUR per month). Deep-dive is needed into this issue type to determine if it’s actually related to the invoices received late or something else.

After exploring and sketching some code with current possibilities for encrypting data using standard Android Keychain tooling is not possible due to tons of problems with keystore stability of the platform, which variates on the vendor and system version, here’s the reports to Google (which was not processed yet):

[https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/158234058|https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/158234058|smart-link]
[https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/157501475|https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/157501475|smart-link] 
[https://github.com/google/tink/issues/321|https://github.com/google/tink/issues/321|smart-link] 

That means using any keystore functionality on Android platform is unreliable and about to drastically increase crash level. 

There’s two solutions which possible to do:


# To keep the storage unencrypted (means as is).
My estimation here is that there’s a really small chance someone can stole token by access to internal storage directory of the app. Some 3rd party apps still possible to do this but it is based on the users decisions: most of the users make a rooting access by their own it is the user’s risk and we cannot be responsible of any user actions.
# To encrypt the data by some hardcoded inside the app key. 
We still can use encryption of storage but based on static key, which will be hardcoded right into the application. There’s no way to encrypt with some dynamic key the data which comes BEFORE user auth, because we don’t have any dynamically provided key at the start of application. Efficiency of this method is also not durable.
# To encrypt data with firebase instance_id key.
It’s possible to encrypt session based data with firebase instance id key but the data which stored outside client session scope will remain unencrypted.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2],

Please find below the external counsel’s advice:

+*Background*+

From the information provided, we understand that Bolt Market periodically launches blanket discount campaigns for products sold through the online market.

From a Portuguese law perspective, these campaigns can be qualified as commercial practices involving *price reductions*, with a view to disposing of stocks, *increasing sales volume* or promoting the launch of a product not previously marketed by the economic agent (*Decree-Law no. 70/2007, of 26 March*, as amended by Decree-Law no. 9/2021, of 29 January).

It is our understanding that the discount campaigns mentioned in your email below are to “attract more consumer eyeballs” and, consequently, increase sales.

+*Analysis*+

Based on the background above, please find our opinion in relation to the questions that you have raised:

# [*End date of the campaign - is it mandatory to mention the end date of the discount campaigns?* |https://www.mlgts.pt/]

Regarding this first question, we clarify that in cases of sale with price reduction, the type of sale, the type of products, the respective percentage of reduction, *as well as the starting date and the duration period of the campaign* must be unequivocally indicated (article 4(1) of Decree-Law no. 70/2007).

Through the knowledge of the start date and duration of the campaign, the consumer will be made aware of the end date. In other words, the consumer must be supplied with information in order to easily determine the end date of the campaign. The safest way to do so is to mention the end date expressly.

# [*Exclusions - do they need to state all the products that are excluded from the discount campaign or can they use a generic legal sentence such as "some products might be excluded from discounts"?*  |https://www.mlgts.pt/]

Regarding this second question, Portuguese law does not state that it is necessary to mention the _specific_ products excluded from the price reduction campaign. However, it does require the identification of the _type_ of products being sold at a reduced price.

Based on these rules, we would say that it is possible to include a disclaimer clarifying that the discount campaign does not apply to certain products. This disclaimer should link to some webpage or other information source whereby the consumer can quickly and easily understand which are the excluded products.

It may be relevant to note also that, under Portuguese law, it is forbidden to sell at a reduced-price products that are acquired _after_ the commencement date of the campaign, even if the price is the same as that charged during the reduction period. In order words, the discount should apply to products already acquired/in stock.

# [*Push notifications – considering that these notifications should be as short as possible, do they need to mention all the discount campaign details (i.e. dates and excluded products) in said push messages?* |https://www.mlgts.pt/]

Concerning the third question, taking into account the applicable legislation, we consider that it is necessary to ensure that the method of sale, the type of products, the respective percentage of reduction, as well as the starting date and duration period of the campaign is information that must necessarily conveyed to the consumers in a clear manner.

Furthermore, it should be noted that misleading’s commercial practices are expressly prohibited under the law . A commercial practice is misleading if it contains false information or if, *although factually correct, for any reason, including overall presentation*, it deceives or is likely to deceive the consumer, or if it causes or is likely to cause the consumer to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise.

Therefore, although it is not expressly stated in the law that push notifications contain the information listed above, it is necessary that the consumer have easy access to this information before proceeding to purchase the product (example: if the push notification only alerts to the price reduction campaign, this notification should refer to the place where the consumer can obtain the rest of the information required by law *before proceeding to purchase the products concerned*). Naturally, as explained above, it is absolutely forbidden for push notifications to mislead the consumer by providing false information or create a perception of something that does not correspond to the truth.

Finally, we inform that if the above information (the type of sale, the type of products, the respective percentage of reduction, as well as the starting date and the duration period of the campaign) is not provided to the consumer in a sale with price reduction, such action is punishable, when committed by a legal person, with a fine that can range between *€ 250* and *€ 30 000*, depending on the severity.

*Response for Portugal*

Based on the background above, please find our opinion in relation to the questions that you have raised:

# [*End date of the campaign - is it mandatory to mention the end date of the discount campaigns?* |https://www.mlgts.pt/]

Regarding this first question, we clarify that in cases of sale with price reduction, the type of sale, the type of products, the respective percentage of reduction, *as well as the starting date and the duration period of the campaign* must be unequivocally indicated (article 4(1) of Decree-Law no. 70/2007).

Through the knowledge of the start date and duration of the campaign, the consumer will be made aware of the end date. In other words, the consumer must be supplied with information in order to easily determine the end date of the campaign. The safest way to do so is to mention the end date expressly.

*2.* [*Exclusions - do they need to state all the products that are excluded from the discount campaign or can they use a generic legal sentence such as "some products might be excluded from discounts"?*  |https://www.mlgts.pt/]

Regarding this second question, Portuguese law does not state that it is necessary to mention the _specific_ products excluded from the price reduction campaign. However, it does require the identification of the _type_ of products being sold at a reduced price.

Based on these rules, we would say that it is possible to include a disclaimer clarifying that the discount campaign does not apply to certain products. This disclaimer should link to some webpage or other information source whereby the consumer can quickly and easily understand which are the excluded products.

It may be relevant to note also that, under Portuguese law, it is forbidden to sell at a reduced-price products that are acquired _after_ the commencement date of the campaign, even if the price is the same as that charged during the reduction period. In order words, the discount should apply to products already acquired/in stock.

*3.* [*Push notifications – considering that these notifications should be as short as possible, do they need to mention all the discount campaign details (i.e. dates and excluded products) in said push messages?* |https://www.mlgts.pt/]

Concerning the third question, taking into account the applicable legislation, we consider that it is necessary to ensure that the method of sale, the type of products, the respective percentage of reduction, as well as the starting date and duration period of the campaign is information that must necessarily conveyed to the consumers in a clear manner.

Furthermore, it should be noted that misleading’s commercial practices are expressly prohibited under the law . A commercial practice is misleading if it contains false information or if, *although factually correct, for any reason, including overall presentation*, it deceives or is likely to deceive the consumer, or if it causes or is likely to cause the consumer to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise.

Therefore, although it is not expressly stated in the law that push notifications contain the information listed above, it is necessary that the consumer have easy access to this information before proceeding to purchase the product (example: if the push notification only alerts to the price reduction campaign, this notification should refer to the place where the consumer can obtain the rest of the information required by law *before proceeding to purchase the products concerned*). Naturally, as explained above, it is absolutely forbidden for push notifications to mislead the consumer by providing false information or create a perception of something that does not correspond to the truth.

Finally, we inform that if the above information (the type of sale, the type of products, the respective percentage of reduction, as well as the starting date and the duration period of the campaign) is not provided to the consumer in a sale with price reduction, such action is punishable, when committed by a legal person, with a fine that can range between *€ 250* and *€ 30 000*, depending on the severity.

# As I wrote in the other ticket as well, according to our Special Terms: _“The Special Terms of the Agreement may be amended by the parties’ agreement in a form reproducible in writing.”_ This means that agreeing on a higher commission as well as any marketing initiatives via e-mail is legally binding, however, please make sure that the Partner has confirmed it with an e-mail and that the e-mail is sent to you by a person authorised to act on behalf of the Partner. In some cases Partner want a separate agreement signed with them and that’s where you can use the document you linked in the other ticket.
# The general principle is that companies are equal parties to negotiate agreements, meaning that if they decide on agreements of 2 years with a 180 days notice period and also the 10% penalty fee, then this should be valid and binding.
# About exclusivity - the term of exclusivity depends on Bolt Food’s market share in PT, however, the general principle is that exclusivity cannot last more than 5 years. For example, in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, where Bolt Food has a bigger market share, we do not recommend exclusivity lasting more than 1 year. Please see below my remarks I have given to the teams:
Notes on items to be considered prior to use of the exclusivity clause:

* It is advisable to limit the length of the exclusivity up to one year. Longer exclusivity should be considered separately and have a specific justification.
* In any communication offering exclusivity specify, that the conclusion of exclusivity is not a pre-condition for concluding the agreement with Bolt.
* Prior to use of exclusivity assess and document that there remains a sufficent number of alternative competitiors/venues to the Partner (who cater for the same customer segment and whose offering is similar) on the market who are not bound by exclusivity (both by Bolt or other platforms). This is to ensure that competing platforms have other available and similar restaurants in order to avoid market foreclosure.
* If feasible, do not conclude exclusivity agreements with leaders of specific segments, but prefer smaller competitors (preferably Partners which have not used platforms before or are entering the market). There is the argument that Bolt invests in promoting the Partner and thereby enhances the competitive situation is strongest.

A lifecycle rule has been added to the cloudfront module.
It’s not possible to create a flag to set or not the lifecycle dynamically due terraform [limitation|https://www.terraform.io/language/expressions/dynamic-blocks]s:

{quote}It is _not_ possible to generate meta-argument blocks such as {{lifecycle}} and {{provisioner}} blocks, since Terraform must process these before it is safe to evaluate expressions.{quote}

The only way to achieve the expected result is duplicate the resource ans set a {{bool}} control flag, the downside is that all resources would be recreate by terraform due the change of a map to an array in the terraform resource control.
